tests.label: Does the same universal JRC equilibrium response survive relaxed galaxy-cluster RAR measurements?
tests.summary: Relaxed clusters require an effective acceleration scale about an order of magnitude above the galaxy branch. The frozen JRC equilibrium has one global a* and positive lambda only reduces the response; finite Jeans-time lag suppresses response and cannot generate the observed cluster excess.
tests.keyMetrics: Cluster effective scales: ~9.5e-10 overall 52-cluster sample; 1.59e-9 relaxed Chandra; 2.02e-9 CLASH. Relative to JRC galaxy-fit a*=1.4775e-10: ~6.4x, 10.8x, 13.7x. Deep-regime acceleration mismatch factors ~2.5-3.7 (~0.40-0.57 dex), versus quoted cluster residual widths ~0.09-0.14 dex.
tests.provenance: Cross-source falsification; sign check of lambda and finite-response terms; no goalpost shift.

tests.label: Can the frozen two-parameter JRC equilibrium law reproduce the published SPARC RAR mean shape without galaxy-specific knobs?
tests.summary: The frozen JRC law tracks the galaxy RAR to ~0.025 dex RMS but is materially worse than the empirical one-parameter RAR as a bin-mean curve; shape compatibility survives because the mismatch is below galaxy-level scatter.
tests.keyMetrics: JRC best a*=1.4775e-10 m/s^2; lambda=4.2516; RMS=0.02495 dex; max|resid|=0.0534 dex; bin-SEM chi2=72.96. Empirical RAR fitted gdagger=1.1711e-10; RMS=0.01570 dex; chi2=33.29; DeltaAIC(JRC-RAR)=+41.66.
tests.provenance: Python nonlinear fit using published bin means; literature source table; frozen lambda>=0.

tests.label: Does the UAC-aligned DESI ShapeFit preference survive official native Full-Modelling galaxy bias/EFT/stochastic nuisance profiling?
tests.summary: Native DESI Full Shape absorbs most of the compressed ShapeFit separation; residual preference is small and localized mainly to QSO.
tests.keyMetrics: FS Δχ²(UAC-LCDM)=-1.159; FS+BAO=-1.358; ≈80.2% of |ShapeFit Δχ²| absorbed; QSO ≈-2.26 while non-QSO tracers sum ≈+1.09.
tests.provenance: closure_json_sha256=d990522e83dfaca5683954a2db89ef89b140700ddd55617cc05c9d110c1e9d64; official DESI inputs/windows/covariance; fixed UAC0P vs matched LCDM.

tests.label: Do tracer-wise DESI full-shape LambdaCDM Omega_m estimates from DR1 galaxies/quasars plus new DR2 Lyalpha full-shape require a redshift slope over constant Omega_m, robust to shared-covariance and leave-one-out stress?
tests.summary: CONSTRAINED: positive Omega_m(z) slope direction reproduces 1.86sigma source result, but constant LambdaCDM remains acceptable and AICc favors constant; removing DR2 Lyalpha drops slope to 0.73sigma.
